## Decisions
- Presets reuse existing model types only (tracks/clips/effects/keyframes) — no new render-graph, persistence, or Inspector seam — so undo/redo, save/round-trip and editing all work for free. Rationale: matches the feature plan's explicit preference ("avoid a separate preset system unless proven necessary") and phases 1–2's own precedent of "registering is the whole change."
- A preset's plate-wide motion (shake/shockwave/blur/fringe/flash) always lives on an adjustment layer stacked *above* the generator overlays — not on the selected clip — so the playhead alone (no selection needed) places the whole thing and everything moves together.
- Playhead = impact frame; all keyframe times are anchored there (absolute timeline time per `AnimatableValue.Shifted` semantics).
- Track reuse: a layer reuses a free (non-overlapping) track above the content floor whose blend mode already matches, so repeated hits share VFX tracks instead of accumulating new ones every insert.
- No fire/explosion plate generator was added — placement hints tell the user to pair with imported alpha stock (step 26 precedent), consistent with the feature plan's explicit "no full simulation" scope guard.

- **Gotcha for future doc-edit scripts:** this repo's git index stores these files as LF (`i/lf`), but Python's `open(..., newline='')` combined with reading a file that turns out to already contain CRLF (or an editor auto-normalizing) can silently write CRLF back out, producing a whole-file diff. Always check `git diff --stat` immediately after any scripted multi-file text edit — a suspiciously large line-count change (thousands of lines for a few sentences) is CRLF/LF drift, fix with `sed -i 's/\r$//' <file>` before committing.
